parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile national framework with a division that adds a school/college facility ban (no enforcement mechanism, no documented arrest). Universal exposures dominate: the 2025 executive order bars trans people from federal single-sex facilities, the foreign ministry restricts passport markers and instructs officers to refuse cases casting doubt on sex (with lifetime fraud ineligibility considered), and eight foreign governments issued travel advisories. Documented immigration-custody abuse (beatings, sexual abuse, forced labour) is severe but contingent. No criminalisation of trans identity exists; federal courts have enjoined several orders, a hate-crime statute and 2020 employment ruling stand, and 33 local ordinances protect. Net: tier-1 universal exposure with partial, contested remedy.

entry_documents.exposure: Foreign ministry stopped processing X markers (Feb 2025); Supreme Court allowed restriction (Nov 2025). Cable directs refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex, with lifetime fraud ineligibility considered for wilful misrepresentation. Travellers report blocked/confiscated passports and being stranded; foreign governments issued advisories over document/data rules.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, has limited waivers and is never automatic; civil-liberties suit pending in national courts; legal-aid FAQ guides documentation strategy.
entry_documents.interaction: Home passport mismatch can trigger refusal, then prolonged secondary screening, then possible immigration custody where documented abuses occur.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: In immigration custody, transgender men reportedly subjected to forced-labour programmes, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. Division facility law carries no enforcement mechanism; no arrest or citation documented under it. A bathroom arrest occurred in a different state/province (Mar 2025, 24h in men's ward).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Division facility law requires willful entry plus refusal to depart, not automatic arrest; trespass charge is a misdemeanour; federal prison conversion-therapy policy reaches citizens/prisoners, not ordinary visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry refusal → detention pipeline converts a document mismatch into custody exposure; record is contingent, not routine.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities nationwide; division requires K-12 and all colleges to assign facilities by birth certificate and use matching birth certificate — universal-exposure rule for campus visits,Visitor use of federal-building restrooms exposed.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division law has no enforcement mechanism and no documented enforcement; single-occupancy restrooms exempt; 29 other state/provinces have no mapped ban, though map notes other sex-definition laws may apply.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility rule reaches every government-funded building the visitor enters regardless of division variation; the federal trespass-crime states are elsewhere, not this division.

care_services.exposure: Division care/sports ban (blockers, hormones, surgery for under-18s) status unresolved after Mar 2025 re-injunction and announced appeal; October 2025 national rule would bar public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 trans care; specialised LGBTQ youth lifeline shut down July 2025.
care_services.protection: Proposed perpetual-counselling adult-care rules were withdrawn Feb 2024 and are not in force; the division care ban was re-enjoined by an appeals court; emergency care denial to visitors not documented.
care_services.interaction: An adult visitor's care access is undocumented rather than restricted; a travelling minor with a parent faces the unresolved state ban interacting with federal funding threats.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy (May 2026) prioritises neutralising groups 'radically pro-transgender'; DOJ memo invokes 'radical gender ideology' among extremist animating ideas; EO directs law enforcement to investigate 'gender ideology' in schools; division stripped trans candidates from ballots (2024) and mandates outing of LGBTQ students (Jan 2025). Poll: 66% back ASAB document rules.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Dossier notes 'radical gender ideology' is never a criterion for the reward, and counterterrorism powers are stated not to target mere disagreement; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity; marriage and employment protections intact.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises the probability and social licence for outing and confrontation, but stops short of naming trans status itself as a target.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division facility law binds all students by birth certificate; Jan 2025 law requires school staff to out LGBTQ students to parents; EO threatens criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; care ban for under-18s in litigation.
minors_guardians.protection: Prosecution threat targets facilitators, not the travelling minor or guardian; marriage recognition and parental rights of trans parents not documented as restricted for visitors; facility law has no enforcement mechanism.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visiting family enrolling or touring schools enters an institutional regime designed to police the minor's identity, but short-term visitors are largely outside the school reporting duties.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Dossier documents no trans-specific killings or attack pattern; national statistics record bias incidents against sexual orientation at one-seventh to one-fifth of single-bias hate incidents; only 23 state/provinces cover gender identity in bias-crime statutes and 33 local ordinances provide the division's practical protection.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 2020 Supreme Court employment ruling and a circuit ruling apply; travel guide advises only routine checking of violence reports; division has no documented anti-trans violence pattern.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Sparse violence record in a well-documented country is mildly positive, but gap in state bias statutes thins recourse if an assault occurs outside the 33 covered municipalities.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Several executive orders blocked or enjoined but unresolved; passport suit pending; DMV August 2026 marker rules are an announcement only; county birth-certificate refusals persist with no identified remedy; several foreign advisories signal unresolved risk.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Federal courts have repeatedly enjoined hostile measures; legal-aid FAQ, equality/identity-document maps and a running risk assessment function; 33 municipal ordinances; employment and marriage protections operative.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Working courts mitigate hostile policy only partially — the document and federal-facility rules currently in force have no demonstrated remedy for an individual traveller.

anchor_checks.comparison: Very similar: routine universal exposure at checkpoints and services from sex-definition rules, discretionary official judgement, documented detention/denial, courts recognising only narrow claims and slow legal aid. Lower than 0.45-A only in lacking an explicit deceptive-presentation statute; comparable on inconsistent enforcement and uncertainty.

Lower than 0.55-B. That anchor's harms stop at secondary screening, refused admission and administrative returns with written reasons and consular notification. Here federal facility exclusion, an entry-refusal/fraud-ineligibility instruction, hostile counterterrorism framing and documented immigration-custody abuse stack on top of the same border friction.

Materially lower than 0.75-C. There, trained border staff, a working tribunal, counsel access and compensation define the worst case. Here the tier-1 federal facility ban and document regime operate without demonstrated individual remedy, and custody abuse is documented — outweighing the analogous rights machinery this dossier also has.

Higher than 0.35-A. That anchor imposes a universal, consistently enforced exclusion register with no real appeal. Here exclusion is not systematic: entry refusal is discretionary and waivable, facilities bans largely lack enforcement mechanisms, no trans-status criminal offence exists, and courts have granted repeated injunctive relief.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces one continuous national layer (facility exclusion from federally funded single-sex spaces, passport/entry screening that invites refusal and a fraud finding, official threat-framing) plus a division layer that adds an unenforced school/college birth-certificate facility rule and narrowing DMV markers — rules visitors rarely touch. Severity is capped: no criminalisation of trans identity, functioning courts repeatedly enjoining hostile measures, hate-crime and employment protections, robust legal-aid and monitoring infrastructure, and no documented trans-specific street violence. What holds the score in Elevated Risk is the tier-1 universal facility/document exposure with no traveller-level remedy, multiplied by documented immigration-custody abuse awaiting anyone funneled into detention, and eight foreign governments judging the risk worth an advisory.
